option.label: Blade hairs arise from small raised bases
option.detail: Inspect the long stiff hairs and their raised papilla-like bases, especially near the ligule. These are blade hairs, not the ligule itself.

option.label: Stem joints lose hairs with age
option.detail: Compare young and older culm nodes on one plant. A formerly bearded node may become nearly hairless; this does not mean every young node is hairless.

option.label: Stolons after close grazing or cutting
option.detail: Gould reports that this tufted historical variety can become somewhat stoloniferous under close grazing or cutting. Confirm an actual surface stem; a low-lying culm alone is insufficient.

option.label: Rhizomes after close grazing or cutting
option.detail: Gould permits some rhizomatous growth under close grazing or cutting. Confirm an underground stem; this does not claim every untreated tuft has rhizomes or an extensive Johnsongrass-like network.

option.label: Flowering branches round below spikelets
option.detail: Inspect the slender flowering branch just BELOW its spikelets. Terete describes its round cross-section, not the shape of the culm or glume.

option.label: Medial groove on terminal rachis joints / pedicels
option.detail: Use magnification on terminal flowering-axis internodes and spikelet pedicels. Gould describes a narrow central groove there, not a pit in a glume.

option.label: Hairs along flowering rachis-joint margins
option.detail: Trace the hairs to the edges of a flowering branch rachis internode. These are not hairs on the lemma, callus or outer glume.

option.label: Hairs along spikelet-pedicel margins
option.detail: Inspect the margins of the stalk supporting the pedicelled spikelet. Do not transfer its hairs to the spikelet surface or the culm node.

option.label: Sessile FIRST glume lacks glandular pit
option.detail: Locate the FIRST (lower) glume of the sessile spikelet. Gould explicitly says no glandular pit or depression; a narrow groove on the rachis is a different organ.

option_additions.subgroup: First glume: sessile versus stalked spikelet

option.label: Sessile FIRST glume has rough margins
option.detail: Inspect the margins of the sessile spikelet's first glume. Roughness is not a claim that every outer glume has the same surface.

option_additions.subgroup: First glume: sessile versus stalked spikelet

option.label: Sessile FIRST glume has stiff hairs below middle
option.detail: Inspect the back of the lower glume of the stalkless spikelet, below its midpoint. Do not confuse these hairs with the pedicel fringe.

option_additions.subgroup: First glume: sessile versus stalked spikelet

option.label: Sessile FIRST glume has a pointed apex
option.detail: Follow the lower glume to its acute tip. The glume tip and the true lemma awn are separate structures.

option_additions.subgroup: First glume: sessile versus stalked spikelet

option.label: Stalked FIRST glume without hairs
option.detail: Find the lower glume of the stalked companion spikelet. Hairless and hairy-below-middle variants are both permitted; this does not assert all sessile glumes are hairless.

option_additions.subgroup: First glume: sessile versus stalked spikelet

option.label: Stalked FIRST glume hairy below middle
option.detail: Inspect the lower half of the first glume of the stalked companion. This is a variable state, separate from hairs on the pedicel and sessile glume.

option_additions.subgroup: First glume: sessile versus stalked spikelet

learner_diagnostic_checks.look: Check the tuft and its grazing/cutting history
learner_diagnostic_checks.check: Gould's var. songarica is tufted, with erect or basally decumbent culms, and can become somewhat stoloniferous or rhizomatous under close grazing or cutting. Do not infer either structure from a low culm alone. Nodes are shortly bearded and become glabrate with age; sheaths are hairless.
learner_diagnostic_checks.compare: H&L p.37 reports no stolons/rhizomes for its account. Preserve the source and management distinction rather than rejecting a source-permitted growth form.
learner_diagnostic_checks.certainty: Exact historical-variety treatment, pp.602/604; no verified local specimen or universal management response.
learner_diagnostic_checks.source: Frank W. Gould (1975), The Grasses of Texas, Bothriochloa ischaemum var. songarica, printed pp. 602 and 604

learner_diagnostic_checks.look: Separate the sessile and stalked FIRST glumes
learner_diagnostic_checks.check: The sessile spikelet is mostly 3–4.5 mm. Its first glume lacks a glandular pit/depression, usually has rough margins and stiff hairs below the middle of its back, and ends in an acute tip. The stalked staminate partner is similar in length but narrower; its first glume may be hairless or hairy below the middle.
learner_diagnostic_checks.compare: The adjacent B. pertusa description has a deep medial glandular pit in the sessile first glume. Do not transfer pitted-bluestem traits into KR or confuse a rachis groove with a glume pit.
learner_diagnostic_checks.certainty: Gould p.604; exact organs and historical variety preserved, not a photo-based species verification.
learner_diagnostic_checks.source: Frank W. Gould (1975), The Grasses of Texas, Bothriochloa ischaemum var. songarica, printed pp. 602 and 604

learner_diagnostic_checks.look: Trace margin hairs and the tiny bent lemma awn
learner_diagnostic_checks.check: Branch rachis internodes and pedicels have marginal cilia, with a narrow central groove at least on the terminal units. Gould gives a geniculate twisted lemma awn mostly 1–1.5 mm; the stalked staminate spikelet is awnless. Blade papilla-based hairs near the ligule are a separate feature.
learner_diagnostic_checks.compare: The inherited FNA-backed record gives 9–17 mm for lemma awns. Gould/Diggs are preferred for the scoped description; keep the larger report visible and do not recode units or call awns deciduous without evidence.
learner_diagnostic_checks.certainty: Published source discrepancy retained; photographs and measured local spikelets not reverified.

non_scoring_context.occasional_culm_length_cm: Over 100 when basally decumbent or trailing; length is not necessarily erect height.
non_scoring_context.exsertion: Inflorescence well above the uppermost leaf.
non_scoring_context.primary_branches: Usually about 2–8; a parenthetical 1 is also printed. No mandatory branch-count minimum is introduced.
non_scoring_context.pedicelled_spikelet: Staminate, awnless, about as long as sessile companion but usually narrower.
non_scoring_context.historical_distribution: Texas regions 2–7; introduced roadside and pasture grass in the account. Not a county-nativity finding.
non_scoring_context.historical_phenology: Mostly July–November, potentially throughout the year under favorable growing conditions.
non_scoring_context.separate_taxon: The B. pertusa entry below describes pitted bluestem, a different taxon. Its ciliate ligule, deep glume pit and other measurements are not assigned to KR.

omissions_not_absences: Gould does not say the KR ligule is ciliate here.
No measured width may be inferred for the greatly reduced top leaf.
Conditional underground stems are not proof of their presence on every tuft.
No evidence here of deciduous KR awns, unlike the Johnsongrass passage.
No floret count inside a single spikelet is supplied here.
